coverage.assessment: Paragraph 5 now states the intensity difficulty and jumps to 'At all events', without the provisional solution or the 'must stop there' that motivates p6. Paragraph 16 loses the 'motion in a universe of motions' bridge into the mind-as-comet analogy (F1, F4).
Pronouns for the new American, the historian and the scientists stay traceable. 'This stationary period' lacks its source antecedent in both drafts; this is treated under F3.
The chapter has no dialogue. The quoted textbook phrases (two kept, within plan) remain correctly framed as quotation.

Figures are intact: 30,000, 234, 300 million, 1843, 1964 and the before-six marker. The squares formula keeps 'for convenience' but loses 'any other formula would do as well'. The comet's 'For convenience' framing is also cut (F2).
The narrator's speculative distance ('If any analogy whatever existed', 'Perhaps even he') survives, and nothing is disclosed prematurely.

The revision removes the historian's self-portrait as one who could never acquire or impart knowledge, and the teacher who failed the generation of 1870. It also cuts the groaned-shrieked-shuddered cadence (F5).

Three links that thread the inertia, phase and jump argument are lost: science's own 'mental inertia', the scientists' reduction to motion, and the common-salt phase change. The medieval evidence is reduced to architecture (F3, F4, F6, F8).
Dependencies 0 and 1 are intact at both ends. The optional Terebratula joke, kept in the first draft and supported by 017's surviving setup, is cut in revision (F7).

strengths: All eight verbatim anchors (V1–V8) survive exactly, including the comet 'defies law' line, the timid Paris gentleman and the 1964 Ara Coeli projection.
The required figures (30,000 and 234 horse-power, three hundred million tons, 1843, 1838/1905) are preserved without invention.
The comet-falls-into-sun image is set up early and repaid in p16's 'Comet of Newton', with the source's 'to suffer dissipation' wording restored.
The 'live wire or a runaway automobile' sentence keeps its long periodic build into the bathetic bomb-doubling punchline.
summary: The revision keeps every verbatim anchor, the required figures, the comet, coal and squares framework, the timid Paris gentleman, the 1964 Ara Coeli projection, and the final jump. Its extra cuts beyond the first draft mainly remove connective and hedging tissue. The intensity problem is now raised and dropped. 'For convenience' framing and the arbitrariness of the squares formula are thinned. The 'mental inertia of science' link is gone, as is the scientists' 'vertiginous' self-reduction that bridges to the comet analogy. Several of Adams's self-deprecating teacher lines and the salt-solution phase image that explains the jump are also lost. There are no blockers, but several small restorations are warranted.
